[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance document defines the mandated UI component system for all React-based frontend applications at Gainwell Technologies.

**The going-in default for all new development is the Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS stack, with TanStack Table as the standard data grid.** This stack covers the full range of standard healthcare UI — forms, navigation, dialogs, data tables, search results, and queues — without commercial licensing, and within the ≤500KB gzipped module budget.

When a module has verified requirements for complex data grids or chart visualisations that this stack cannot meet, **Kendo UI for React** is the approved solution. How Kendo is introduced depends on where in the delivery lifecycle the requirement arises:

- **Greenfield with complex requirements known upfront:** Build the module on Kendo from the start alongside Tailwind CSS. Do not implement the standard Shadcn/UI stack and then replace it.
- **Existing Shadcn/UI application with a new complex grid or chart requirement:** Drop Kendo in as a targeted component alongside the existing stack. Do not rework the surrounding UI — the Kendo Grid or Kendo Chart component is added only where needed; everything else remains unchanged.

This guidance applies to all new application development — shell applications, micro-frontend remote modules, and standalone applications — after the technology role is determined per [GUID-APP-TEC-001](../frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md).
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

Following this guidance ensures:

- Consistent visual language and accessible behaviour across all product UIs without per-team divergence in component approaches
- WCAG 2.2 AA compliance achievable from the component layer up — not retrofitted
- No external commercial component licensing cost for standard UI (Radix UI, Shadcn/UI, Tailwind CSS, TanStack Table are all open source MIT)
- Bundle size within the ≤500KB gzipped per-module target — Radix UI and Shadcn/UI components are tree-shakeable and pay-per-use
- Teams own their component code — Shadcn/UI's copy-into-codebase model eliminates upstream breaking change risk

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#business-drivers]

#### Business Drivers

- **ASP.NET Migration**: The migration from Telerik/DevExpress server controls to React requires a React component library equivalent. The target must support healthcare-domain components (member cards, claim grids, provider listings, eligibility displays) built on accessible primitives — not a general-purpose library with opinionated styling.
- **HIPAA and Federal Accessibility**: Section 508 and WCAG 2.2 AA are contractual requirements for all state MMIS implementations. Component behaviour — focus management, ARIA roles, keyboard navigation — must be correct from the outset. Retrofitting accessibility onto opinionated styled libraries costs significantly more than building on compliant headless primitives.
- **Brand Consistency Across State Implementations**: Gainwell serves 50+ state Medicaid agencies, each potentially requiring distinct theming. A design system built on unstyled Radix UI primitives — styled to the Gainwell UX standard via the `@gainwell/design-system` layer — can be re-themed per state via CSS variables with zero component logic changes. Developers consume the Gainwell-themed components, not raw primitives. Material UI or Kendo require overriding a pre-existing design opinion.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#strategic-alignment]

#### Strategic Alignment

The [Enterprise Micro-Frontend Architecture CRB](../../../../governance/crb-submissions/enterprise-micro-frontend-architecture-crb.md) explicitly selected a custom design system built on Radix UI primitives over Material UI and Ant Design, citing branding control and healthcare-specific component requirements. [STD-TEC-NXT-003](../../../../standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md) mandates Shadcn/UI, Radix UI, and Tailwind CSS as the component and styling standard for all Next.js applications.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#the-component-layering-model]

#### The Component Layering Model

The enterprise UI system is a deliberate hierarchy — not a single library:

```
@gainwell/design-system          ← healthcare domain components
                                   (ClaimGrid, MemberCard, EligibilityBadge,
                                    AuthorizationWorkflow, ProviderCard)
         ↓ composed from
Shadcn/UI components             ← general UI compositions
                                   (Dialog, Combobox, Table, DataTable,
                                    Command, Calendar, Toast, Sheet)
         ↓ built on
Radix UI primitives              ← accessible, unstyled behaviour
                                   (focus management, ARIA roles,
                                    keyboard navigation, WAI-ARIA patterns)
         ↓ styled with
Tailwind CSS + CSS Modules       ← all visual output; design tokens via
                                   CSS variables; component-scoped overrides
```

Each layer has a distinct responsibility. Developers building product features primarily interact with the top two layers. The Radix UI and Tailwind layers are infrastructure — they provide the accessibility and styling foundations automatically.

| Material UI | Opinionated styled | ~1.2MB bundle; Google Material Design styling conflicts with Gainwell branding; CSS-in-JS (Emotion) conflicts with Tailwind utility approach |

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#principle-1-accessibility-from-the-primitive-layer]

#### Principle 1: Accessibility from the Primitive Layer

**Description:** All interactive component behaviour — focus management, ARIA roles, keyboard navigation, screen reader announcements — must be handled at the Radix UI primitive layer. Application developers do not implement these from scratch.

**Rationale:** WCAG 2.2 AA is a contractual requirement. Radix UI's primitives implement the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide patterns correctly and are continuously updated for new WCAG criteria. Building accessibility into the primitive layer means every Shadcn/UI component and every `@gainwell/design-system` component built on Radix inherits correct accessible behaviour without per-feature accessibility work.

**WCAG 2.2 coverage via Radix UI:**

- **2.4.11 Focus Appearance** — Radix manages focus ring visibility; Tailwind `focus-visible:ring-*` classes style it to meet contrast and size thresholds
- **2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured** — Radix Dialog and Sheet handle z-index and scroll management
- **2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)** — enforced via Tailwind utility classes on all interactive elements (`min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]` as a design token)
- **4.1.3 Status Messages** — Radix Toast provides ARIA live region announcements

**Application:** When a new interactive component is needed that does not exist in Shadcn/UI, build it on the appropriate Radix UI primitive (or React Aria for complex patterns). Do not implement ARIA attributes manually without a Radix primitive underlying the component.

page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#principle-3-shadcnui-components-are-owned-code]

#### Principle 3: Shadcn/UI Components Are Owned Code

**Description:** Shadcn/UI components are initialised into the codebase via CLI (`npx shadcn@latest add button`) as source files — not installed as an npm package dependency. The team owns and controls every line of each component.

**Rationale:** Unlike an npm dependency, Shadcn/UI components do not impose upstream breaking changes at version upgrade. They do not add to `node_modules` bundle size. They can be modified for healthcare-specific behaviour (e.g., adding PHI-safe ARIA labels to a Dialog) without forking a library. This is the single most important maintainability advantage of the Shadcn/UI model for a healthcare codebase with strict change control processes.

**Application:**

```bash
# Add components as needed — each becomes a file in src/components/ui/
npx shadcn@latest add dialog
npx shadcn@latest add data-table
npx shadcn@latest add combobox
npx shadcn@latest add calendar
```

Resulting file structure:

```
src/
  components/
    ui/                    ← Shadcn/UI components (owned code)
      button.tsx
      dialog.tsx
      data-table.tsx
      input.tsx
    domain/                ← @gainwell/design-system components
      claim-grid.tsx
      member-card.tsx
      eligibility-badge.tsx
```

New Shadcn/UI versions are adopted selectively — copy the updated component source, review the diff, merge any local modifications. No `npm update` breakage risk.

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#approach-1-standard-ui-components-shadcnui--radix-ui]

#### Approach 1: Standard UI Components (Shadcn/UI + Radix UI)

**When to Use:** All interactive UI — dialogs, drawers, popovers, dropdowns, comboboxes, date pickers, tabs, toasts, tooltips, form controls, navigation menus.

**Implementation:**

```tsx
// Dialog — Radix UI under the hood, Shadcn/UI API surface, Tailwind styling
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
} from '@/components/ui/dialog';

export function ClaimAdjudicationDialog({ claimId, open, onOpenChange }) {
  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
      <DialogContent className="max-w-2xl">
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Adjudicate Claim</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>
            Review and process claim {claimId}
          </DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        {/* Content */}
        <DialogFooter>
          <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => onOpenChange(false)}>Cancel</Button>
          <Button type="submit">Submit Decision</Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

**WCAG 2.2 behaviour provided automatically by Radix:**

- Focus trapping within dialog when open
- Return focus to trigger element on close
- `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` wired to DialogTitle and DialogDescription
- Escape key dismissal
- Scroll lock on body while open

#### Approach 2: Data Grid — TanStack Table (Default Going-In Approach)

**When to Use:** All standard product data grids — claim lists, provider search results, member eligibility tables, payment history, authorisation queues. Any grid with row counts under ~20,000 rows or where complex enterprise features (cell editing, Excel export, server-side virtual scroll) are not required.

TanStack Table is the **first choice** for all data grids. Do not evaluate Kendo Grid until TanStack Table has been assessed against the specific requirement.

See [Data Grid and Chart Visualisation Selection](#data-grid-and-chart-visualisation-selection) for the full decision framework.

page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#approach-3a-data-grid--charts--kendo-ui-greenfield-complex-requirements-known-upfront]

#### Approach 3a: Data Grid / Charts — Kendo UI (Greenfield, Complex Requirements Known Upfront)

**When to Use:** A new module is being built where complex data grid or chart visualisation requirements are known before development begins — e.g., 50,000+ row grids with inline editing, Excel export, or enterprise charts (treemaps, financial charts, drill-down dashboards).

**Pattern:** Build the module on Kendo from the start, styled via Kendo's CSS custom property API aligned to the Tailwind design token system. Do not first implement the Shadcn/UI + TanStack Table stack and then replace it — this creates unnecessary rework.

**Why Tailwind and Shadcn/UI are still required alongside Kendo — not replaced by it:**

Kendo UI is licensed and scoped to the grid or chart surface only. It does not replace the application's surrounding UI layer. Every module that uses Kendo still requires a full UI system for navigation, page layout, forms, dialogs, filters, buttons, tooltips, notifications, and all other interactive surfaces — none of which are covered by the Kendo Grid or Kendo Charts components. Replacing Tailwind and Shadcn/UI with Kendo's general-purpose components (KendoButton, KendoInput, KendoDialog, etc.) would:

- **Expand the Kendo license scope to the entire module** — the commercial license cost and dependency footprint grow from one targeted component to every interactive element on every page
- **Lose the `@gainwell/design-system` integration** — all Gainwell-standard domain components (MemberCard, ClaimGrid, EligibilityBadge, AuthorizationWorkflow) are built on the Shadcn/UI + Radix + Tailwind stack and cannot be consumed in a module that has abandoned that foundation
- **Break visual consistency with the micro-frontend shell** — the shell and all other remote modules use Tailwind design tokens. A module styled entirely with Kendo's theme system would visually diverge from the application shell regardless of CSS custom property mapping
- **Eliminate WCAG compliance from the primitive layer** — Shadcn/UI and Radix UI provide WAI-ARIA patterns, focus management, and keyboard navigation for all standard interactive components. Kendo's general-purpose components do not have equivalent accessible primitive infrastructure for healthcare UI patterns

The architectural boundary is deliberate: **Kendo owns the grid or chart interior; Tailwind and Shadcn/UI own everything else.**

> **CSS conflict awareness:** Tailwind CSS and Kendo's Bootstrap-derived CSS can conflict via Tailwind's global preflight reset. This must be mitigated before development begins. See the [Tailwind Preflight Conflict Mitigation](#integration-with-shadcnui--tailwind-css-both-patterns) section for the required scoped wrapper approach.

Requires an ADR before starting. See [Data Grid and Chart Visualisation Selection](#data-grid-and-chart-visualisation-selection) for the full greenfield Kendo pattern.

---
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#approach-3b-data-grid--charts--kendo-ui-drop-in-to-existing-shadcnui-application]

#### Approach 3b: Data Grid / Charts — Kendo UI (Drop-In to Existing Shadcn/UI Application)

**When to Use:** An existing application already built on Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS receives a new requirement for a complex grid or chart that TanStack Table cannot meet.

**Pattern:** Add the Kendo Grid or Kendo Chart component only where needed — as a targeted drop-in within the existing module. The surrounding UI (navigation, forms, dialogs, filters, other grids) remains on the Shadcn/UI stack unchanged. Do not rework or replace the existing component system.

This is the most common path for established products adding complex reporting or processing features. Kendo components and Shadcn/UI components coexist in the same module. See [Data Grid and Chart Visualisation Selection](#data-grid-and-chart-visualisation-selection) for integration details.

> **CSS conflict awareness:** Tailwind CSS and Kendo's Bootstrap-derived CSS can conflict via Tailwind's global preflight reset. If the module does not already have the preflight mitigation in place, it must be applied before adding Kendo. See the [Tailwind Preflight Conflict Mitigation](#integration-with-shadcnui--tailwind-css-both-patterns) section for the required scoped wrapper approach.

---
page_texts.29: [strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#best-practice-2-target-size-enforcement-for-wcag-258] #### Best Practice 2: Target Size Enforcement for WCAG 2.5.8 **Description:** All interactive elements must meet the WCAG 2.2 minimum target size of 24×24px. Icon-only buttons must be at minimum 44×44px (exceeding the 24px minimum to meet usability as well as compliance standards). On tablets and mobile devices, the recommended touch target size is **44×44px**, aligned with [WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced, Level AAA)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced) and consistent with Apple Human Interface Guidelines and Google Material Design recommendations to ensure reliable touch interaction for users with motor impairments. ```tsx // ✅ CORRECT: Icon button meets 44×44px minimum // ❌ WRONG: 16×16px icon-only button ``` Define standard sizes in Tailwind config so they are not duplicated per-component: ```typescript // tailwind.config.ts extend: { height: { 'touch': '44px' }, width: { 'touch': '44px' }, minHeight: { 'touch': '44px' }, minWidth: { 'touch': '44px' }, } ``` ---

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#best-practice-3-phi-safe-aria-labels]

#### Best Practice 3: PHI-Safe ARIA Labels

**Description:** ARIA labels and descriptions on components must use static strings or opaque identifiers — never PHI directly in accessible name attributes.

**Rationale:** Screen readers announce ARIA label content audibly. PHI in an ARIA label is both a HIPAA concern (audible in open environments) and a data exposure risk if accessibility tree content is captured.

```tsx
// ✅ CORRECT: Opaque claim ID + generic label
<Button aria-label={`Adjudicate claim ${claimId}`}>
  Adjudicate
</Button>

// ❌ WRONG: PHI in accessible name
<Button aria-label={`Process claim for ${member.firstName} ${member.lastName} DOB ${member.dob}`}>
  Process
</Button>
```

| Phase | Objectives | Key Activities | Deliverables |

| Phase 1: Initialise | Set up component system | Run Shadcn/UI init; configure Tailwind with design tokens; establish `cn()` utility; add Radix UI peer dependencies | `components/ui/` directory; `tailwind.config.ts` with token system; `globals.css` with CSS variables |

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#installation]

#### Installation

```bash
# Tailwind CSS (already included in Next.js 14+ with App Router)
npm install tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer

# Shadcn/UI initialisation
npx shadcn@latest init
# Prompts: Style (Default), Base colour (Neutral/Slate), CSS variables (Yes)

# Radix UI (installed automatically per-component by Shadcn/UI CLI)
# Direct install only if using Radix primitives directly (not via Shadcn/UI)
npm install @radix-ui/react-dialog @radix-ui/react-popover

# TanStack Table
npm install @tanstack/react-table

# TanStack Virtual (if virtualisation needed for TanStack Table)
npm install @tanstack/react-virtual

# cn() utility dependencies (installed by Shadcn/UI init)
npm install clsx tailwind-merge
```

#### Decision Point: Which Component Do I Need?

```
Is this a healthcare domain component (MemberCard, ClaimGrid, EligibilityBadge)?
  ├── YES → Use @gainwell/design-system
  └── NO ↓

Is this a standard interactive UI component (Dialog, Dropdown, Combobox, Tabs)?
  ├── YES → Use Shadcn/UI (add via CLI if not already in codebase)
  └── NO ↓

Is this a complex interaction not in Shadcn/UI (e.g., complex date range picker, drag-drop)?
  ├── YES → Build on Radix UI primitive or React Aria component
  └── NO ↓

Is this a data grid or chart visualisation?
  └── See Data Grid and Chart Visualisation Selection section below
```

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#full-ui-component-stack-reference]

#### Full UI Component Stack Reference

| Layer | Tool | Purpose | Install Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design tokens | Tailwind CSS + CSS variables | Colours, spacing, radius, typography | Tailwind config + `globals.css` |
| General UI components | Shadcn/UI | Dialog, Drawer, Dropdown, Combobox, Calendar, Toast, Table | `npx shadcn@latest add <component>` |
| Accessible primitives | Radix UI | Underlying ARIA/focus behaviour for all Shadcn/UI components | Installed automatically by Shadcn/UI CLI |
| Complex interactions | React Aria (Adobe) | Date range pickers, data grid keyboard nav, drag-and-drop where Radix has no primitive | `npm install react-aria-components` |
| Component-scoped styles | CSS Modules | Animations, pseudo-element content not expressible in Tailwind | `.module.css` alongside component |
| Data grid (default) | TanStack Table | Sortable, filterable, paginated tables | `npm install @tanstack/react-table` |
| Data grid (complex exception) | Kendo UI for React Grid | 50,000+ row virtualisation, inline cell editing, Excel export | `npm install @progress/kendo-react-grid` + licensed |
| Chart visualisation (complex exception) | Kendo UI for React Charts | Enterprise charts — drill-down, financial, treemap, scatter, OHLC | `npm install @progress/kendo-react-charts` + licensed |
| Utility | clsx + tailwind-merge (`cn()`) | Conditional class merging without conflicts | Installed by Shadcn/UI init |

### Exception: Kendo UI for React

Kendo UI for React is the **approved solution for complex data grids and chart visualisations** that exceed TanStack Table's scope. It is **not the default** — the Shadcn/UI + TanStack Table stack must be assessed first.

Kendo is approved for two distinct situations. Which pattern applies depends on when in the delivery lifecycle the complex requirement is identified.

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#pattern-1-greenfield--complex-requirements-known-upfront]

#### Pattern 1: Greenfield — Complex Requirements Known Upfront

When a new module is being built and complex grid or chart requirements are confirmed before development begins, **build the module on Kendo from the start**.

**Do not:** Implement Shadcn/UI + TanStack Table and then replace it once the complexity becomes apparent. That path creates rework and technical debt.

**Do:** Initialise the module with Kendo Grid or Kendo Charts as the component for those requirements. All other UI in the module (navigation, forms, dialogs, filters, status indicators) still uses Shadcn/UI + Tailwind CSS. Kendo handles only the grid or chart surface.

**Qualification — complex grid (one or more must apply):**

| Criterion | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Row count | Routinely >50,000 rows requiring built-in row AND column virtualisation |
| Editing model | Inline cell editing with server-side validation integration — not row-level forms |
| Export requirement | Excel `.xlsx` export is a confirmed business requirement deliverable to end users |

**Qualification — complex charts (one or more must apply):**

| Criterion | Examples |
|---|---|
| Chart type not achievable with standard SVG/Canvas libraries | Treemap, OHLC financial chart, drill-down hierarchy, Sankey/flow diagram |
| Interactive drill-down with server data binding | Click-to-drill charts linked to live data source |
| Chart + grid data binding | Kendo Grid and Kendo Chart sharing a single DataSource with selection sync |

**Process:**

1. Create an ADR in `decisions/application/` documenting the specific requirement and why TanStack Table / lightweight SVG libraries cannot meet it
2. Obtain Architecture Review Board awareness
3. Procurement approval for Kendo UI React license (~$800–1,200/developer/year through Progress)
4. Scope the license to only the affected module
5. Include a dependency security assessment (CVE scan via `npm audit`, Snyk, or equivalent) in the ADR per [STD-SEC-APP-001 §3.6](../../../../standards/security/application/STD-SEC-APP-001-application-security.md); no Critical or High unmitigated CVEs are permitted at time of adoption

page_texts.45:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#pattern-2-retrofit--drop-in-to-an-existing-shadcnui-application]

#### Pattern 2: Retrofit — Drop-In to an Existing Shadcn/UI Application

When an existing application already built on Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS receives a **new requirement** for a complex grid or chart, **drop Kendo in as a targeted component** alongside the existing stack.

**Do not:** Rework or replace the surrounding UI. The existing navigation, forms, dialogs, filters, and standard grids remain on Shadcn/UI. Kendo is added only for the specific grid or chart feature that requires it.

This is the most common path for established products adding complex reporting, remittance processing, or analytics dashboards.

**Key integration rules for drop-in:**

- Kendo Grid or Kendo Chart is rendered inside a standard Shadcn/UI layout container — the page shell, sidebar, breadcrumbs, header, and filter controls remain unchanged
- Kendo's CSS custom properties are scoped to the component boundary (e.g., `.k-grid` or `.k-chart` selector) — they do not leak into the Shadcn/UI layout
- Radix UI Dropdown, Dialog, and Button components continue to work inside Kendo custom cell renderers and toolbar slots
- Data fetching uses the same TanStack Query hooks already in the application — Kendo Grid is wired to the same server state, not a separate fetch layer
- Bundle impact: code-split the Kendo component into a child route so the primary module entry point stays within ≤500KB

**Process:** Same ADR and licence procurement as Pattern 1. The ADR additionally documents that the surrounding UI is not being replaced.

---
page_texts.47:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#bundle-size-consideration]

#### Bundle Size Consideration

`@progress/kendo-react-grid` and `@progress/kendo-react-charts` are each ~350–500KB gzipped. Adding either to a remote module will push that module's bundle against or over the ≤500KB limit. The ADR must address the bundle budget impact and demonstrate that the Kendo component is code-split into a child route so the primary module entry point remains within budget.

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#decision-framework]

### Decision Framework

```
Is this a data grid or chart?
  ├── CHART → See chart branch below
  └── GRID ↓

─── GRID ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Start with TanStack Table. Does the grid requirement exceed TanStack Table's scope?
(>50,000 rows needing built-in virtualisation, OR inline cell editing,
 OR Excel export to end users)
  ├── NO → Use TanStack Table (+ TanStack Virtual if >5,000 rows)
  └── YES — Complex requirement confirmed ↓

      Is this a greenfield module (new build, Kendo requirement known upfront)?
        ├── YES → Pattern 1: Build the module with Kendo Grid from the start
        │         (Shadcn/UI still used for all non-grid UI; ADR required)
        └── NO — Existing Shadcn/UI application ↓

              → Pattern 2: Drop Kendo Grid in alongside the existing stack
                (surrounding UI unchanged; Kendo scoped to the grid feature;
                 code-split onto child route; ADR required)

─── CHART ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Is the chart a standard type (bar, line, pie, area, stacked)?
  ├── YES → Use a lightweight SVG/Canvas library (Recharts, Victory, Visx)
  │         scoped to the module — no commercial license needed
  └── NO — Complex chart requirement ↓
      (Treemap, OHLC financial, drill-down hierarchy, Grid+Chart DataSource sync)

      Is this a greenfield module (new build, Kendo requirement known upfront)?
        ├── YES → Pattern 1: Build the module with Kendo Charts from the start
        │         (Shadcn/UI still used for all non-chart UI; ADR required)
        └── NO — Existing Shadcn/UI application ↓

              → Pattern 2: Drop Kendo Chart in alongside the existing stack
                (surrounding UI unchanged; Kendo scoped to the chart feature;
                 code-split onto child route; ADR required)
```

### Use Case 1: Claims Search Results Grid

**Scenario:** Claims list with sort by status/date, multi-select for batch adjudication, row-click to detail drawer, 200–2,000 rows typical.

**Guidance Application:** TanStack Table + Shadcn/UI DataTable. Sorting and filtering client-side. Row selection via TanStack row selection model. Detail drawer using Radix-backed Shadcn/UI Sheet component. Batch action bar appears when rows are selected using `table.getSelectedRowModel().rows`.

**Success Factors:** Bundle impact ~50KB; WCAG 2.2 keyboard navigation implemented on `<tr>` elements; Radix Dropdown in action column with correct `sr-only` label.

### Use Case 3: Remittance Detail Grid (Kendo Pattern 1 — Greenfield, Complex Requirements Known Upfront)

**Scenario:** A new Remittance Processing module is being built from scratch. Requirements are defined before development starts: 200,000 line items, inline adjustment code editing, freeze first two columns, row grouping by payer, Excel export of selected rows required by state contract.

**Guidance Application:** Complex grid requirements are known at project initiation — this is Pattern 1. The Remittance module is built with Kendo Grid as the grid component from the start. Page layout, navigation, toolbar, filter controls, and status indicators outside the grid use Shadcn/UI + Tailwind CSS as normal. ADR documents: row count (200K), inline cell editing (adjustment codes), Excel export (state contractual deliverable). Kendo CSS custom properties scoped to `.k-grid` override aligned to Tailwind tokens. Kendo grid code-split onto `/remittance/detail` child route; primary module entry stays within ≤500KB.

**Success Factors:** ADR approved before development starts; Kendo not used for the module's non-grid UI; theme vars mapped to Tailwind tokens; Radix Dropdown components work in Kendo custom cell renderers; bundle split verified with Webpack Bundle Analyzer.

[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#use-case-4-population-health-dashboard-charts-kendo-pattern-2--drop-in-to-existing-app]

### Use Case 4: Population Health Dashboard Charts (Kendo Pattern 2 — Drop-In to Existing App)

**Scenario:** The Population Health module is live and built on Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS. A new product requirement adds a drill-down regional health outcomes dashboard — hierarchical treemap with click-to-drill, and a member cohort trend chart with 5-year actuals overlaid against plan targets. Standard bar/line chart libraries (Recharts) cannot meet these chart types.

**Guidance Application:** This is Pattern 2 — an existing Shadcn/UI application receives a complex chart requirement. The page layout, navigation, member search, existing TanStack Table grids, and all Shadcn/UI components in the module are left entirely unchanged. Kendo Charts (`@progress/kendo-react-charts`) is added only for the two new chart components. The charts are rendered inside standard Shadcn/UI `Card` wrappers within the existing layout. The chart feature is code-split onto a `/analytics/outcomes` child route to isolate the ≤500KB budget impact. ADR documents why Recharts cannot support treemap + server-bound drill-down without significant custom engineering.

**Success Factors:** Surrounding UI untouched; Kendo Charts scoped to the two new chart components only; Kendo CSS vars scoped to `.k-chart` selector; existing TanStack Table grids and Shadcn/UI components continue unchanged; ADR approved; bundle split isolates Kendo from main module entry.

page_texts.55:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#why-cant-our-team-use-material-ui]

### "Why can't our team use Material UI?"

**Short answer:** Material UI is not approved for new development at Gainwell Technologies. This is an enterprise architectural decision, not a team-level preference. The formal decision record is [ADR-APP-003](../../../../decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md) (accepted 2026-04-08).

**Technical reasons** (sourced from ADR-APP-003 and the analysis in this guidance document):

1. **Bundle size**: Material UI carries a ~1.2MB bundle (see §Technical Context — What Was Rejected and Why, above). The enterprise ≤500KB gzipped per-module budget (established in ADR-APP-002) is immediately violated. The approved Shadcn/UI stack copies components into your codebase — there is no runtime library import and no bundle overhead from the component layer.

2. **CSS-in-JS (Emotion) conflicts with Tailwind CSS**: MUI relies on the Emotion CSS-in-JS runtime to apply styles at runtime. Emotion-injected styles and Tailwind utility classes cannot be cleanly co-located without CSS specificity conflicts that break both systems. The enterprise design token strategy (GUID-APP-UI-001) is implemented via CSS custom properties consumed by Tailwind — it is not compatible with a competing CSS-in-JS runtime.

3. **Material Design visual language does not match Gainwell healthcare branding**: MUI implements Google's Material Design aesthetic — a consumer-facing design language. Adapting it to Gainwell's healthcare product UI requires learning and overriding MUI's proprietary `sx` prop and `ThemeProvider` API, rather than applying standard CSS variable overrides. Gainwell's multi-state deployment model (50+ state tenants, each potentially requiring distinct branding) needs a theming system based on CSS variables — not a library-specific ThemeProvider.

4. **Accessibility cannot be directly fixed**: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance in MUI is dependent on MUI's release cadence. When an accessibility defect is found, your team cannot fix it without forking the library. Gainwell has contractual Section 508 and WCAG 2.2 AA obligations for all state MMIS implementations. Radix UI provides WAI-ARIA-correct primitives that your team owns and can remediate directly.

5. **Formal governance-body decision**: The Enterprise MFE Architecture CRB explicitly selected a custom design system built on Radix UI primitives over Material UI, citing branding control and healthcare-specific component requirements. This is a CRB decision, not an open question.

---
page_texts.56:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#what-if-we-already-have-mui-components-in-our-codebase]

### "What if we already have MUI components in our codebase?"

**You are not required to migrate existing MUI components immediately.** However, **no new MUI components may be added** — all new component work must use the approved Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS stack.

For planned migration of existing MUI components to the enterprise design system, use:

**[PTN-APP-MFE-005 — Design System Migration Pattern](../../../../patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md)**

This pattern defines:
- Incremental migration strategies that allow existing MUI components to coexist temporarily with new Shadcn/UI components during a transition period
- Component-level mapping from common MUI components to their Shadcn/UI + Radix UI equivalents
- The `@gainwell/design-system` package as the long-term target for healthcare domain components

Work the migration into your product backlog. The priority and timeline are determined by your team and product roadmap, not mandated by this guidance — but the constraint that no new MUI adoption occurs in the meantime is firm.

---
page_texts.57:
[strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md#how-do-we-request-an-exception]

### "How do we request an exception?"

If you have a specific, documented technical requirement that the approved Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS stack genuinely cannot meet, you may request an exception through the formal process:

1. **Submit a formal exception request to the Architecture Review Board (ARB)** per the ARB process in [`governance/processes/architecture-governance.md`](../../../../governance/processes/architecture-governance.md)
2. **Document the specific requirement** that cannot be satisfied by the approved stack — for example, a specific UI pattern, interaction model, or integration constraint
3. **Demonstrate you have genuinely assessed the approved stack** and explain concretely why it does not address the requirement
4. **Accept the ARB decision as binding** — the ARB may approve an exception, require modifications to the proposal, or uphold the rejection

**What is not sufficient for an exception:**
- Team familiarity or prior experience with Material UI
- Preference for MUI's API or component model
- Time or effort to learn Shadcn/UI

The formal ruling for Material UI rejections is [ARD-APP-003a](../../../../decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md). Share that document with your team lead or requesting stakeholder for the full technical rationale and exception pathway.
